subject: Next steps: Deployment mode & migration plan (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@luminalabs.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-25T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: deployment mode needs & migration paths

Hi Samir / Ava

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the recommended next steps so we can evaluate the right deployment mode for Lumina Labs: Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, or Private VPC/on-prem.

Key points I captured:
- Current stack: You're using a legacy GPU cluster for inference (internal endpoints) and also have some traffic routed through a third-party LLM API for burst capacity.
- Landing goals: reduce per-token cost, improve 95th percentile latency, and centralize observability across models.
- Security: must support SOC2 evidence for audit and option for VPC or on-prem due to PHI in some workflows (pilot initially non-PHI).
- Timing: goal to start a migration POC in Q3, full rollout in Q4 if POC meets latency/cost targets.

Recommendation (quick):
- POC: Start with Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) to mirror your current throughput while we validate latency and cost.
- Parallel test: Route non-sensitive traffic to Redwood Hosted API to compare unit economics and operator overhead.
- Long-term: Evaluate Private VPC if you need strict network isolation or an on-prem package for PHI.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll share a short migration checklist + SOC2 evidence stub (attached).
2) Rishi (SE) to scope the POC benchmarking tests (model sizes, sequence lengths, concurrency).
3) Schedule a 60-min technical kickoff for next Tue or Wed, please advise availability.

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — super helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- For the POC we want to validate both latency at 99th percentile (our SLAs are tight) and cost per 1M tokens comparing our self-hosted setup vs your Dedicated offering.
- We have an internal security review that will want the SOC2 artifact and a short list of network controls for Private VPC.
- Timeline: Tue next week looks good for the kickoff, prefer morning PST.

Two asks before the kickoff:
1) Can Rishi share an example POC test plan (metrics, scripts)?
2) Can you confirm whether Dedicated supports automatic autoscaling bursts for unexpected traffic spikes?

Samir

Hi Samir / team

Appreciate the clarity. I attached a brief POC test plan and sketch of the benchmarking script we typically use. Highlights:
- Tests we'll run: 99th and 95th latency under fixed concurrency (1, 4, 8 workers), throughput ramp, and cost-per-token measurement using identical model weights.
- Models: start with 7B and 13B variants (you mentioned heavier prompts up to ~1k tokens).
- Data routing: we'll demonstrate a hybrid route (hosted for low-risk traffic, Dedicated for sensitive flows) to compare both economics and operational overhead.
- Dedicated autoscaling: yes - Dedicated supports configurable autoscale policies and a burst capacity option that can add short-lived instances to handle spikes (we'll include parameters in the POC plan).

Proposed availability for kickoff: Tue 2026-06-30 09:00 PST (60 min). If that doesn't work, Wed 2026-07-01 10:00 PST also open.

Neha will share the SOC2 artifact and a short VPC/network control checklist in a follow-up.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
